**Step 1 — Scene:** A main plate of rice with what appears to be chicken curry, potato chunks, and a little carrot. The separate salad and fruit plates are excluded, as requested; so are the separate dressing cup and water.

**Step 2 — Vessel:** The main dinner plate looks approximately **24 cm across**. Area = 3.14 × 12² = **452 cm²**.

**Steps 3–7 — Items, coverage, volume, weight, and energy:** The curry ingredients are estimated separately. Sauce includes the visible coating and its cooking fat; no additional oil is assumed.

| Item | Plate area | Area × height = gross volume | Bulk density | Estimated grams | kcal/100 g | kcal |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Cooked rice | 25% | 113 cm² × 1.5 cm = 170 ml | 0.8 | 136 | 130 | 177 |
| Chicken pieces | 23% | 104 cm² × 1.6 cm = 166 ml | 0.95 | 158 | 180 | 284 |
| Potato chunks | 14% | 63 cm² × 1.7 cm = 107 ml | 0.65 | 70 | 85 | 60 |
| Carrot pieces | 3% | 14 cm² × 1 cm = 14 ml | 0.6 | 8 | 35 | 3 |
| Curry sauce/coating | 6% | 27 cm² × 0.6 cm = 16 ml | 1.0 | 16 | 130 | 21 |

**Coverage check:** 25 + 23 + 14 + 3 + 6 = **71%**, consistent with the visible food and exposed rim. Sauce coverage represents its additional footprint rather than counting the coated pieces twice.

**Step 8 — Sanity check:** Approximately **388 g and 545 kcal** is plausible for this moderately heaped main plate. The largest uncertainties are the chicken identification and the amount of fat in the curry sauce.
